summary:
The fix for R2-m1 / O-011 works and I found nothing new to file. The only code change since my last review is the C-007 cleanup check and its header comment in tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1. Get-Scratches is gone, and nothing else in the tree still refers to it.

Lines 363-370 now pull this run's own scratch folder name (32 hex characters) out of its output with `[regex]::Matches`, then check two things: exactly one copy is named, and that copy no longer exists on disk.

- **My reproduction now passes.** I re-ran C-007 while a stand-in folder appeared in the shared %TEMP%\fsa-window-mutants 10 s into the run. Every check was ok, including 'the run named one scratch copy (389e1493...)' and 'the scratch copy was removed'. It ended PASSED: C-007, exit 0, with the stand-in still there at the end, as intended. I then deleted the stand-in; no scratch copies or FsAnalyser.App processes were left.
- **The check can still fail.** I ran the same matching on made-up lines with a real GUID folder created under the shared folder:
  - copy left behind: 1 named, and it still exists, so the check fails;
  - two copies named: count 2, so the check fails;
  - no copy named: count 0, so the check fails.
- **Edge cases:**
  - Copy names are lowercase hex from ToString('N'), so a case-sensitive match is right.
  - The child process shares TEMP with the parent, so joining the name to $ScratchParent gives the same folder.
  - A fresh copy has no obj folder, so its output always includes a 'Restored ...' line and a '-> ...' line.
  - A run that fails before building names no copy, and that already fails.
  - If Remove-Scratch cannot delete the copy, it only prints a message, but the copy is still on disk, so C-007 fails.

The C-007 header comment matches the new behaviour. tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1, the acceptance test and the app code have not changed since the build commit, so the earlier runs still describe them: the real `-Mutant EndingObeysSkip` kill, `-Mutant All` with 9/9 killed, and the real compile-error and crash runs that were not counted as kills.

Second round: Nothing new to file in round two. The only change since the last clean pass is C-007's cleanup check (tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1:363-370). I tried to break it with inputs the run's output could contain:
- **Case and form of the name.** New-Scratch builds folder names with [guid]::ToString('N'), which is always lowercase 32-character hex. The parent and child processes share TEMP, and TEMP here is not an 8.3 short path, so the path the build prints and Join-Path $ScratchParent point at the same folder.
- **Line wrapping.** The build output goes through a pipe, not a console, so it is not wrapped. The long 'Restored ...' and '-> ...' paths came through whole in every real run, and the regex matched in my run with a concurrent stand-in folder.
- **Other names in the output.** Remove-Scratch's '(could not remove <root>, ...)' message names the copy with no backslash after it, so the regex skips it. The same GUID is already named by the build lines, and a copy that is left behind still fails Test-Path.
- **Partial failures.** If the run fails before building (stale anchor, no SDK), no copy is named and 'the run named one scratch copy' fails. C-007 is already red in that case, so this is correct. Two copies named, or none, fail the count check. A copy left on disk fails the existence check. I confirmed all three on made-up lines against a real GUID folder, and removed that folder afterwards.
- **Error records.** Lines are turned into plain strings before matching, so a line from stderr cannot break `[regex]::Matches`.

Everything else in the tree is unchanged since the lap that already went over it this way.

obligations.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-064-EndingObeysSkipMutant.Tests.ps1 is unchanged since the build commit. It exited 0 when I ran it and when the engine ran it.
tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1:29, the ValidateSet includes 'EndingObeysSkip'. Unchanged; C-001 passed.
tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1:78-84: Case 'L-002', File $MainWindow. Unchanged; C-002 passed.
The Find at tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1:79 matches once, inside ShowFinalTopLevel (MainWindow.xaml.cs:338). Unchanged; C-003 passed.
The Replace at :80 adds '&& !_skipNextRefresh'. In the C-007 re-run, L-002 ended with the skip armed and topLevel.final 'False'.
Fail/MayFail/Expect at :81-83, applied by Test-CaseMutant :194-203. In the C-007 re-run the harness matched its Fail pattern and nothing else.
The roster at tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1:254 includes EndingObeysSkip. Unchanged; the earlier real -Mutant All run killed all 9.

The C-007 re-run just now: the real -Mutant EndingObeysSkip run exits 0 and published the app in a scratch copy, L-002 was reported FAILED on topLevel.final 'False', and the real source hash is unchanged.
Test-C008 is unchanged (tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1:373+). My earlier C-008 run passed on an unmutated New-Scratch copy.
The harness has not changed. Earlier real runs through Test-CaseMutant: a compile error (CS0103, publish failed) gave KILLED=False, and a throw at the ending (exit 70, no report) gave KILLED=False.

tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1:363-370 takes this run's GUID from its own lines, requires exactly one, and checks with Test-Path that it is gone. Get-Scratches has been removed (grep finds no reference). My re-run of the concurrent stand-in reproduction passes (exit 0, stand-in still present), and made-up lines with the copy left behind, two copies, or none are all caught.

Unchanged. Test-C002 reads $CaseMutants['EndingObeysSkip'] from the loaded harness.
Unchanged. Test-C003 runs the anchor once, twice and reformatted through the real Set-Mutation.
Unchanged. Test-C004 compiles the guard text word for word with _skipNextRefresh=true and a new final snapshot.
Unchanged. Test-C005 runs the real Test-CaseMutant on L-002 output that matches the real run's lines.
Unchanged. Test-C006 evaluates the real $names statement with $Mutant='All'.
Test-C007 runs the real -Mutant EndingObeysSkip end to end, and its cleanup check now looks at this run's own copy. I re-ran it with a concurrent stand-in folder: exit 0, all checks ok.

C-005's made-up publish-failure and crash output, plus my earlier real compile-error and crash runs through Test-CaseMutant. Neither was counted killed.
